findings.body:
**`-0` passes the walk, but `JSON.stringify` writes it as `0`.**

`src/shared/jsonLossless.ts:21` rejects only non-finite numbers. `JSON.stringify(-0)` returns `"0"`, so the journal line loses the sign. Replay then rebuilds `0`, not the `-0` the run produced. This is the same kind of silent divergence the header comment says the walk is meant to catch. Math results such as `Math.round(-0.4)` or `0 * -1` can produce `-0`.

Either reject `-0`, or document it as an accepted normalization next to the `undefined`-member note in the header. If you reject it, check whether callers can legitimately produce `-0`. Also check whether the other `assertJsonLossless` walks (`src/cli/output.ts` and the frozen `src/kernel/runner.ts`) need the same change. The retrieved learning says shared validation changes must update those walks together in a coordinated post-freeze migration.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
     case 'number':
       if (!Number.isFinite(value)) throw new Error(`non-finite number ${String(value)}`);
+      if (Object.is(value, -0)) throw new Error("negative zero — JSON.stringify writes it as '0'");
       return;
```
</details>

Based on learnings: `src/cli/output.ts` `assertJsonLossless` deliberately mirrors the frozen phase-1 `src/kernel/runner.ts` walk. Changes to shared validation behavior must update both walks in a coordinated migration.
